name: Corradini 2014: LTP primed burst, left temporal lobe, rotating CW (20 min)
origin: Corradini 2014, MA thesis in Persinger's laboratory (Laurentian University), using Murphy's Shiva solenoids and hippocampal 'LTP' pattern
summary: The left-hemisphere arm of Corradini's (2014) memory-consolidation study in Persinger's lab: the Shiva 'LTP' primed-burst pattern stepping clockwise around four coils over the left temporal lobe for 20 min at 1 uT, between immediate and delayed recall of short stories. Corradini reported better story retention after left-sided fields than after sham (4 people per arm; 'accommodating 60% of the variance').
notes: Corradini (2014, MA thesis) applied the Shiva software's hippocampal 'LTP' pattern at 1 uT for 20 min over one temporal lobe at a time (left, right or sham; 4, 4 and 3 people) between immediate and delayed recall, through 8 Shiva solenoids (4 per side) activated one at a time, clockwise on the left and counter-clockwise on the right; the person scoring the recalls was blind to the condition. She modelled the study on Richards, Persinger & Koren (1996), who reported about twice as many accurate narrative details 10 days after left-hemisphere LTP fields. This file is the left arm; persinger-corradini-2014-ltp-right is the other, and the app's Blind option gives the sham. Corradini reported better story retention after left-sided fields than after sham (eta2 = 0.60), no story gain after right-sided fields, and better recall of an unrelated word list after either field than after sham (eta2 = 0.37). Pattern: her Figure 2 caption gives positive values only (127-256), 1-ms points and 150 ms from a primer pulse to 4 further pulses (Rose et al. 1988, primed-burst potentiation); measured on the figure at that scale, each pulse is about 5 ms wide and the 4 pulses are about 14-15 ms apart (onset to onset), so this file uses 5-point pulses starting at 0, 150, 164, 178 and 192 ms (an estimate from the plot). Five such primed bursts fill 1 s (the lab's '1 s pulse of 5 trains', Delparte & Persinger 2007), then 4 s of silence (Murphy's standard latency between Shakti/Shiva signal repeats); the five trains and the pause are assumptions, since the Shiva file is proprietary. Coil geometry follows Collins (2014) for the same hardware: on each side a square of 4 coils 5 cm apart vertically and 8 cm horizontally (Corradini's photos show the same, slightly tilted square), here FT7, FC5h, CPP5h, TPP7 and FT8, FC6h, CPP6h, TPP8 (a fitted inference, lower edge just above the ear). The thesis gives only the direction: the step order (upper front, upper back, lower back, lower front, viewed from outside the head) is an inference, and 200 ms per coil is chosen so that each coil receives whole primed bursts (a primer and its 4 pulses on the same coil). Unlike persinger-ltp-pleasantness-left (Persinger 1994, two static coils), the pattern steps around four coils. An unpublished MA thesis with 4 people per field arm, never independently replicated; in rats the lab's LTP-type fields impaired consolidation (Delparte & Persinger 2007; McKay & Persinger 2000), so do not treat this as a memory enhancer. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop on headache or distress.
setting: Dark, quiet room, eyes closed (the lab used a shielded acoustic chamber). Before the program, have someone read you two short stories (and a 15-word list) and say or write down everything you remember right away (immediate recall); run the 20-min program with eyes closed; then recall them again (delayed recall) and score both against the text.
schedule: One session per arm in the original (between groups). For a self-test, run the left, right and sham (Blind) arms on separate days with a different story each time, in counterbalanced order, and have the recalls scored blind.
